summary: Both supported operations require information from every wrapped integer, and the implementation processes each value only once while constructing its numeric or textual result.

optimality.argument: For Add, changing any one of the n input integers can change the answer, so every value must be incorporated. For String, every one of the n elements must appear in the output. Reduction or joining visits each element once, matching that lower bound.

replacement_checks.evidence: Neither the numeric total nor the required serialized array can be correct for arbitrary inputs without accounting for all n elements.
The constructor performs one reduction, valueOf returns the cached total, and toString performs one join over the stored array.
Cases cover empty, single-element, unequal-length, zero-valued, maximum-valued, addition, and string-conversion inputs.
